author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows under its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it. It is the inverse view of the veterinarian directory.
acceptance_criteria: GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name
each specialty is listed with the veterinarians holding it
each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for example "Helen Leary")
a veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page
every specialty renders on one page, with no pagination
a specialty held by no veterinarian is listed with no veterinarian named under it
specialties, and the veterinarians under each, render in a stable order
a clinic that knows no specialty renders an empty directory rather than a failure
non_goals: managing veterinarians or specialties through the application (NG-2, unchanged)
a navigation entry or a link to the page from any other page
searching or filtering the specialty directory
notes: Owner decisions quoted in the intake-decision at handoff.jsonl line 1: "A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2 is unchanged)." and "The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come as a follow-up request." No Non-Goals row changed, so no scope_overrides. Two unstated choices taken as the narrowest reading and recorded as Open Questions in docs/prd.md: a stable render order (mirrors REQ-VET-001 edge case 1), and the deferred visible entry point. author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The specialty directory is the vet feature package extended along patterns already in force, with one thin new layer. Three pieces: a SpecialtyRepository (Spring Data lookup repository, exact analogue of owner/PetTypeRepository), a SpecialtyDirectory value object holding the inversion and the render order, and a SpecialtyController serving one unpaged page at /specialties.html into a new templates/vets/specialtyList.html. No new package, no new dependency, no schema change: the specialties table and the vet_specialties join table already exist, and Vet.getSpecialties() is EAGER, so holders come from the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(). Every specialty the clinic knows -- including one no veterinarian holds -- is only reachable through a repository over Specialty itself, which is why the new repository is needed; deriving the list from vets would drop unheld specialties. Specialty carries no inverse mapping to Vet: the join is done in memory over two reads. Recorded in docs/system-design.md Contracts (three new rows, REQ-VET-003 added to Vet, Specialty, VetRepository) and in the Invariants paragraph above that table.
integration_points: Specialty read boundary: SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one read returning all specialties. Test double: a hand-written stub implementing the interface, supplied to the @WebMvcTest slice as a @TestConfiguration @Bean (testing-principles.md Mocking Policy -- hand-written doubles before a mock framework).

Veterinarian read boundary: the directory reads holders through the existing VetRepository.findAll(). Test double: a hand-written stub implementing VetRepository (two methods), same @TestConfiguration seam. The @MockitoBean stub in the existing VetControllerTests stays as it is; it is not the model for the new tests.

HTTP transport boundary: MockMvc drives GET /specialties.html through real dispatch and view resolution. It is the one sanctioned framework stub (CLAUDE.md Testing Strategy; testing-principles.md Mocking Policy).
Domain boundary: SpecialtyDirectory is constructed from plain collections and has no framework dependency. Its unit test uses real Vet and Specialty instances -- no double at this seam.
Presentation: templates/vets/specialtyList.html replaces fragments/layout with a menu key matching no nav entry, so no navigation item appears (prd-entry non-goal 2).

patterns.description: lookup-entity Spring Data repository returning rows in name order -- the shape SpecialtyRepository copies
controller reads repository, puts one attribute on the Model, returns a view name; SpecialtyController is the same shape without the pagination helper
table page replacing fragments/layout, all wording via #{} keys; specialtyList.html mirrors it with specialty rows and no pagination block
@WebMvcTest + MockMvc + model/view assertions -- reuse the slice shape, replace the @MockitoBean collaborator with hand-written stubs
Value object row: SpecialtyDirectory is immutable and equal by value; the framework never instantiates it, so the persistence-entity exception does not apply and the closed properties bind in full

risks.risk: Putting the specialty-to-holders inversion, the ordering, or the full-name formatting in the controller
risks.mitigation: All three live in SpecialtyDirectory; the controller binds, delegates, selects the view. architecture-principles.md Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: a new rule added to a controller is a fresh violation, not covered by the existing deviation

risks.risk: Render order taken from the database and diverging per vendor -- the same class of defect as the PostgreSQL case-sensitive owner search
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory applies an explicit comparator over the values it received: specialties by name, holders by last name then first name then identity. Repository-side ordering is a convenience, never the guarantee (system-design.md Known Defects)

risks.risk: A new message key missing from one of the eleven bundles, or literal text in the template
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing keys where they fit (specialties, name, none); add any new key to all eleven bundles. I18nPropertiesSyncTest enforces both halves at build time (REQ-LANG-002)
Leave it uncached. The vet cache has no eviction configured and that is an unsettled question (system-design.md Open Questions from the Survey, item 5); a second cache widens it

risks.risk: A new HTTP endpoint widens the exposed surface
risks.mitigation: GET only, no path variable, no query parameter, no bound form, no mutation, and Thymeleaf default escaping on rendered names. security-principles.md Realization, Widening the exposed surface row: what it exposes is stated in the Contracts row

risks.risk: An empty clinic or a specialty held by nobody producing a failure or a blank page
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory over an empty specialty collection yields an empty listing, and an entry with no holders renders as the specialty alone. Both are unit-testable without the web layer

notes: Verdict is minor rather than new: every pattern used is already in force (Repository, Web controller, Value object), and the only delta is one thin type plus a route. Design writes were limited to three Contracts rows, three Implements updates, one Invariants sentence group, and one Package Structure word. || No ADR: the choice to join in memory rather than add an inverse @ManyToMany(mappedBy) on Specialty is contained by this slice and reverses no recorded decision (adr-template -- a choice a single slice contains gets a clause, not an ADR). The rejected alternative would put a second EAGER many-to-many on a shared entity for one read view. It is recorded as a state clause in system-design.md instead. || SpecialtyDirectory entries should carry the specialty name and holder full names as text rather than the entities, so the type is equal by value and the template stays presentation-only. vetList.html concatenates the full name in the template today; the new page moves that formatting into the tested core rather than copying the template concatenation. || Route address /specialties.html is the owner's, quoted in the intake-decision at line 1; docs/prd.md delegates the address to system-design.md Contracts, where the SpecialtyController row now names it. || No IntelliJ MCP oracle in this dispatch's tool list, so the covering-code claims rest on file reads and grep over the vet package and docs/ -- the weaker basis. Verified directly: no SpecialtyRepository, no SpecialtyController, and no template other than vetList.html exists under the vet feature today. || No design-doc-autofix records in the handoff log; autofix audit skipped.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Not verified against the NVD: this project configures no OWASP Dependency-Check plugin (no dependencyCheck in build.gradle), and the reviewer has no network access, so no CVE match ran in this review. The change set adds no dependency and changes no version, so the supply-chain surface is identical to the last pass; the resolved framework versions to close the check against elsewhere (CI or a human) are Spring Boot 4.1.1 and the io.spring.dependency-management 1.1.7 BOM, per build.gradle:5-6. Reported as not run, not as clean.

Robustness, not a security defect -- SpecialtyDirectory.java:183-188 dereferences three nullable columns without a guard: Comparator.comparing(Specialty::getName) at :183, and .comparing(Vet::getLastName).thenComparing(Vet::getFirstName) at :185-187. src/main/resources/db/h2/schema.sql:12-13 and :19 declare vets.first_name, vets.last_name, and specialties.name all nullable, so a row seeded with a null name makes the request throw NullPointerException and land on the error page, which renders the exception message (system-design.md Known Defects). The NPE text carries no sensitive value, and there is no application write path for vets or specialties (NG-2), so the attacker path is conjectural and the severity does not support a fix-routable finding. Worth noting as pattern divergence rather than exposure: getId at :188 is already nullsLast-guarded in the same comparator chain, and the neighboring vetList.html renders a null name as the text "null" instead of failing. Consider nullsLast on the two name comparators if the class is revisited.
approved_aspects: Cross-site scripting (security-principles.md Realization, XSS row): every value the new page renders goes through Thymeleaf's escaping th:text -- specialtyList.html:11 (${listing.specialtyName}), :13 (${holderName + ' '}), and the #{} message keys. No th:utext, no __${...}__ preprocessing, no inline script, no external resource, no href anywhere in the template (grep for utext, __${, javascript:, onclick, <script>, http:// over specialtyList.html returns nothing). Holder names are formatted in Java and rendered as text, never as markup.

Injection into data access: SpecialtyRepository's one @Query is a fixed JPQL literal with no parameter and no concatenation; no request-derived value reaches it. The route takes no path variable, no query parameter, and no request body, so no untrusted string enters the persistence layer at all.

Widening the exposed surface (Realization row): one GET route, read-only, no mutation, no management endpoint touched. What it exposes -- the specialty names and veterinarian full names already published by /vets.html -- is stated in the new docs/system-design.md Contracts row for SpecialtyController. No actuator exposure change. The absent authentication is the recorded demonstration baseline (system-design.md Security Context) and is not a finding here.
Mass assignment: SpecialtyController binds nothing -- no @ModelAttribute, no form-backed type, no identifier from the request -- so the disallow-list requirement has no surface to apply to.
Least privilege at the data boundary: the new read carries @Transactional(readOnly = true), matching VetRepository and PetTypeRepository.

Concurrency: SpecialtyController is a stateless singleton holding only two repository references. SpecialtyDirectory and SpecialtyListing are records that List.copyOf both lists at construction, so the model attribute handed to the view is deeply immutable. SpecialtyDirectory.of only reads the @Cacheable("vets") collection -- stream().sorted() copies rather than sorts in place -- so the shared cached list is never mutated by the new path.

Resource use: no unbounded growth introduced. The vet roster read is the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(); the specialty read is a small unpaged lookup table, and the unpaged page is the product decision recorded in the prd-entry. No file handle, no stream, no executor, no network call is opened.

Credentials and logging: the diff adds no credential, no connection string, no URL, and no log statement; grep over the new vet sources for Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec(, enableDefaultTyping/JsonTypeInfo, FileWriter, new Random, System.out/System.err, and /tmp/ returns nothing. No new exception message is constructed, so nothing new can reach the error page that renders exception text.

Supply chain: build.gradle is not in the change set -- no dependency added, removed, or version-bumped, and the nohttp plain-HTTP check is untouched. Test doubles are hand-written stubs, adding no test-scope dependency either.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Purely additive: three new classes, one new template, two new test classes, all inside the vet package, plus doc rows; no existing source file is modified, one new read-only GET route is added, and the only shared state touched is the cached vet collection, which is read and stream-copied rather than sorted in place.

semantic_surprise.note: The comparators in SpecialtyDirectory are where the surprises sit: specialties are ordered by name alone, so two specialties sharing a name fall back to the query row order, which is weaker than the collation-independence the new system-design paragraph claims; and the name accessors are unguarded while getId is nullsLast-guarded in the same chain, so a null name throws where the neighboring vet list renders the text null.

test_adequacy.note: Seven unit tests over real Vet and Specialty instances cover every acceptance criterion and all three PRD edge cases, and the two controller tests render the real template through MockMvc against hand-written repository stubs, asserting page content plus the negative that a specialty-less vet never appears; the ordering tests feed deliberately arbitrary input, so they would fail against an implementation that merely passed the input order through.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four planned reviewers approved with zero findings, but the security approval carries two recommendations: the dependency CVE check is reported as not run rather than clean because the project configures no dependency-check plugin and the reviewer had no network, and the null-name NPE path is logged as robustness divergence deliberately left unfixed.

scope_deviation.note: No consultations, no design revisions, and the single build retry is a planned partial-artifact checkpoint at the end of TDD cycle 2 rather than a failing gate; the diff matches the requirement stated surface, including the recorded non-goal that the page gets no navigation entry.

rationale: Additive, well-tested, and unanimously approved, so read narrowly. Open the two comparators in SpecialtyDirectory: name-only specialty ordering does not fully deliver the collation-independence the design paragraph now claims, and the name accessors are unguarded where getId is not. The security approval also reports the CVE check as not run.
